prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1996 replaces the check with a dedicated `acceptsMediaType()` parser that correctly handles Accept-header semantics: case-insensitivity, `;q=` parameter stripping, and explicit exclusion of entries with `q=0` (which per HTTP semantics means the client is explicitly refusing that media type). #2046's diff (visible portion) does a plain `acceptHeader?.includes('application/json')` substring check with no q-value handling, so it would incorrectly accept a request that sends `Accept: application/json;q=0` (an explicit refusal) as if the client accepted JSON. Same file/function targeted, so only one should land — #1996's implementation covers the edge cases #2046 misses.

clusters.pick_reason: #1996 replaces the check with a dedicated `acceptsMediaType()` parser that correctly handles Accept-header semantics: case-insensitivity, `;q=` parameter stripping, and explicit exclusion of entries with `q=0` (which per HTTP semantics means the client is explicitly refusing that media type). #2046's diff (visible portion) does a plain `acceptHeader?.includes('application/json')` substring check with no q-value handling, so it would incorrectly accept a request that sends `Accept: application/json;q=0` (an explicit refusal) as if the client accepted JSON. Same file/function targeted, so only one should land — #1996's implementation covers the edge cases #2046 misses.

members.title: chore(client): normalize trailing slashes in discovery paths
members.author: raashish1601
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2215: Both rewrite the trailing-slash stripping logic in buildWellKnownPath() at the exact same lines (replacing the old `if (pathname.endsWith('/')) pathname = pathname.slice(0,-1)` block), so they will merge-conflict on the identical hunk. #2214 (chore) generalizes the strip to a regex `/\/+$/` to handle multiple trailing slashes (e.g. 'foo//'), touching this logic in both buildWellKnownPath and buildDiscoveryUrls. #2215 (fix) extracts the same regex-based stripping into a shared normalizeDiscoveryPath() helper used by buildWellKnownPath, and additionally fixes shouldAttemptFallback(), which still compared pathname === '/' even though the existing (pre-PR) stripping already collapsed a root pathname of '/' to '' before it reached that check -- meaning the root-path fallback-skip branch was dead code prior to #2215. #2215's helper reproduces #2214's multi-slash fix as a side effect while also fixing the separate, actually-impactful root-fallback bug that #2214 leaves unaddressed.
